title: Add invocation latency variance explorer and alert convergence
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context and motivation: Production teams have strong per-route P99 SLOs but poor visibility into why a small subset of invocations generate long latencies and disproportionate token cost. This PR introduces a metric family and dashboard to expose latency variance and phase-level dispersion, and implements an alert convergence layer that reduces duplicate alerts across related routes by merging them when their sampled trace affinity is high. The goal is to help oncall prioritize root causes (kernel GPU stalls, KV-cache misses, request phase skew) instead of chasing noisy duplicate alerts.

What this changes (high-level):
- New metrics: rwd.invocation.latency.variance_ms, rwd.invocation.latency.phase_dispersion, rwd.invocation.latency.tail_skew, rwd.invocation.token_cost.skew (instrumented at the invocation aggregator; values are percentiles + slab histograms).
- Sampling: correlated high-variance trace sampler that biases to retain ~95% of high-variance invocations while keeping overall sampling budget constant. Implemented in tracing/high_variance_sampler.
- Alerting: alert_convergence component that computes pairwise sample overlap (Jaccard-like) across active alerts and suppresses lower-priority duplicates for a convergence window. Configurable via repo-level alert rules.
- Dashboards: latency variance heatmap, route matrix with pairwise convergence scores, tail sample explorer (drill into retained traces), and an oncall playbook doc (docs/observability/variance_playbook.md).
- Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for metric derivation and alert convergence logic; microbenchmarks for sampler overhead.

Commits (summary):
- 3f7c9b2: instrument latency variance and phase dispersion metrics at invocation aggregator
- b2a1d44: add high-variance correlated trace sampler and sampling config knobs
- 9d5e2a1: implement alert_convergence engine and policy config; add unit tests
- f8a7c33: add dashboards and UI components for variance heatmap and tail explorer
- 2c3b9f0: docs: onboarding playbook and runbook; tweak alert thresholds after local validation

Files changed (high-level):
- src/telemetry/metrics/latency_variance.go: metric derivation, slab histogram rollups, labels (route, tenant, model, phase).
- src/tracing/sampler/high_variance_sampler.go: trace retention policy; deterministic seeding for reproducible dev traces.
- pkg/alerts/alert_convergence.go: pairwise overlap logic, priority rules, and suppression window.
- infra/dashboards/latency_variance.jsonnet + webapp components: UI panels and query templates.
- docs/observability/variance_playbook.md: runbook describing how to interpret variance signals and remediate common causes.

Review conversation (high level):
- Diego: requested tighter bounds on the slab histogram memory usage and a flag to opt out tenants with very high cardinality. Action: added cardinality gate and a sampled rollup instead of full histogram for opt-out tenants.
- Priya: asked for an SLO impact analysis and whether alert suppression can hide real cross-tenant incidents. Action: added a conservative suppression rule that never reduces alerts for tenant-isolated incidents and added an integration test that simulates multi-tenant skew.
- Samira: requested clearer dashboard queries and a column for 'observed root cause' where operators can tag known causes. Action: added a UI tag and persisted annotations to the dashboard JSON.
- CI: initial lint failure on JS build due to a TS type in TailSampleExplorer; fixed and re-ran. All checks passing at merge.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Canary rollout to staging for 72 hours with sampler enabled at 10% traffic and metrics exported to metrics-staging.
- Monitor dashboard and verify that the sampler retains >90% of high-variance traces while overall retention rate stays within quota.
- Gradual ramp to production 25% -> 75% -> 100% across two weeks with alert_convergence in "observe" mode for the first week (no suppression, only annotations), then enable suppression conservatively.

Operational notes and follow-ups:
- Added alert_convergence config under /infra/alerts/config to allow product teams to opt-out or tune convergence windows per org.
- Follow-up tasks (Linear): ENG-4392 calibrate slab boundaries for short vs long token invocations; ENG-4410 integrate variance metrics with Optimize recommendations.

Merge details: Squash merge to main after approvals from Diego and Priya. Merged by Priya Raman on 2025-11-12. CI status green.

Release notes: Adds invocation latency variance metrics, a variance heatmap dashboard, a tail-sample explorer UI, a high-variance trace sampler, and an alert convergence engine to reduce duplicate alerts across related routes. No breaking changes.
